quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, what should you do?

options.text: Look toward the center of the road.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This prevents you from being blinded by the bright lights and lets you see enough of the road to stay safe. Do not retaliate by keeping your bright lights on.

questions.question: A driver is tailgating you on a two-lane road. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down gradually to let the tailgater pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.
Brake suddenly, then resume your original speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually to let the tailgater pass you.
questions.explanation: Slow down gradually. This encourages the tailgater to pass you. If possible, move to a different lane first. Do not brake suddenly or speed up.

questions.question: You are in the center lane of an expressway and are being passed on both sides. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: Move to the right lane. On expressways with four or more lanes, use the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than traffic, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is turning left, what lane may they use?

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. You should expect to see a bicyclist using the left lane when turning left.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a dangerous driving situation?

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Be aware of everything around your vehicle. Watch the front, sides, and rear constantly. This helps you spot problems early so you can change your speed or position safely.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: When safe, gradually steer back onto the road.
Turn back onto the road immediately.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: When safe, gradually steer back onto the road.
questions.explanation: Slow down and do not turn sharply back onto the road. Check for traffic, then gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: You are turning left at an intersection. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a walk signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all vehicles moving toward you on their green light.

questions.question: You are entering the interstate. You find a gap, match traffic speed, and signal. What is the next step?

options.text: Expect traffic to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to completely clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Merge into the gap when it is safe. Be alert and do not expect other drivers to clear the lane for you.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: Lanes go in opposite directions and passing is allowed.
Lanes go in the same direction and passing is allowed.
Lanes go in the same direction and passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes go in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: A solid white line means you cannot cross it to pass or change lanes. White lines separate traffic going the same direction.

questions.question: How far ahead should you look to avoid sudden braking or turning?

options.text: Three seconds ahead
10 seconds ahead
15 seconds ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 seconds ahead
questions.explanation: Look at least 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle. This gives you time to see hazards and make safe decisions. It also gives drivers behind you time to react to your movements.

questions.question: Your car is skidding to the left. Which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Do not turn the steering wheel.
Turn left.
Turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid. Take your foot off the gas and stay off the brakes. Note: If you have anti-lock brakes, apply them firmly and steer straight ahead.

questions.question: An oncoming car's headlights are too bright. How do you avoid the glare?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep your eyes on the centerline.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Glance briefly at the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights. Then look ahead again to track the other vehicle's position.

questions.question: When should you increase your distance from the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, create extra space ahead. Slow down gradually or move to another lane. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Traffic is merging from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you of conditions just ahead. This sign tells you that traffic will merge onto your road from the right. Be ready to let them in safely.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with its siren and lights on while you are in an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right and stop before leaving the intersection.
Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren, finish crossing the intersection first. Then pull to the right side and stop. You must always yield to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using lights or sirens.

questions.question: You are turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. Which lane should you turn into?

options.text: Any lane.
The first lane.
The second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn from your current lane into the first available legal lane. When turning from a two-way street to a one-way street, turn into the first lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
Winding road with curves ahead.
Slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangerous conditions. This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when wet. Drive carefully in wet conditions.

questions.question: When is it legal to turn left at a red light after stopping?

options.text: When turning from a two-way street onto a two-way street.
When turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After stopping completely, you may turn left at a red light only when you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs prohibiting this turn.

questions.question: Your car is skidding out of control. What should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Do not use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, do not brake. Keep steering until the car is under control again and moving safely.

questions.question: As you come to the top of a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up a little.
Be ready to stop if needed.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill. A car could be stopped just out of sight. Slow down when approaching hills and curves so you can stop if necessary.

questions.question: Your vehicle has Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS). How should you stop on snow or ice?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Do not use the brakes and let the car drift to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and hold it when stopping on snow or ice. The ABS will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: Traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph. How can you least likely have an accident?

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic around you (as long as it is within the speed limit). Vehicles moving at the same speed cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if there is no oncoming traffic. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: In bad weather, what should you do?

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid sudden braking and sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when rain first starts. What should you do?

options.text: Do not make fast turns or stops.
Test your tires' grip while going uphill.
Look closer to your vehicle instead of farther ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make fast turns or stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads do not give your tires good grip. Drive slower on wet roads than on dry roads. Avoid quick turns and hard braking to prevent skidding.
